title: Business scanner: interface direction
question: Library catalog is the assigned proposal. Choose it, an alternate, or re-roll; this reviews the design brief and does not start implementation or scanning.

options.label: Library catalog
options.lineage: Library discovery catalogs and indexed reference records
options.thesis: Find a business through precise facets, then inspect its evidence in one consistent record.
options.viewport: Area/category/opportunity facets at left, a dense record list at center, selected website/source evidence at right, and Preview scan in the scope bar.
options.risk: Catalog density needs careful priority on mobile; a missing source field must never resemble a confirmed absence.
options.path: Choose area and category, preview a permitted scan, retrieve records, inspect evidence, save a prospect and export permitted fields.
options.signature: Selecting a record keeps the facet path and row position while synchronizing evidence and the optional map.
options.reach: The same catalog grammar carries prospect lists, scan histories and source permissions; mobile uses facets plus full-page records.

raised.raise: Every record keeps a stable visible identity and one precise hierarchy across results, evidence and history; labels stay explicit.
Selection reveals a complete evidence record without losing list context, with equivalent keyboard and touch behavior.
The index earns real information density: aligned columns, tabular counts and honest unknowns, with no invented data spectacle.

options.label: Agency research workbook
options.lineage: Agency prospect worksheets and research ledgers
options.thesis: A working table turns website evidence into deliberate prospect decisions.
options.viewport: A compact scope bar and statistics strip lead directly into a sortable business table with opportunity reasons and an adjacent evidence pane.
options.risk: Familiar and efficient, but also close to where many prospecting dashboards naturally land.
options.path: Filter the table, inspect evidence, edit prospect status/notes and generate a permitted export.
options.signature: Review next advances through a filtered queue while retaining the same evidence layout.
options.reach: Scans and source settings reuse the table/control grammar; mobile records expose the same decisions.

options.label: Terminal wayfinding
options.lineage: Airport signs and successive decision points
options.thesis: The next permitted action is always clearly signed.
options.viewport: A yellow scope band leads area → category → preview; below it explicit result/evidence routes keep the current destination visible.
options.case: Product clarity holds for setup and blocked-source decisions; audience identification is weaker for daily agency research.
options.risk: Large sign bands can crowd dense records; numerical scope replaces invented travel times and standard forms remain labeled.

options.label: Scan gate board
options.lineage: Boarding documents and live gate-status boards
options.thesis: A bounded scan scope sits beside a live board of evidence and exceptions.
options.viewport: A labeled scan-scope panel sits beside fixed-column discoveries and task states; a changed result stays visibly marked until reviewed.
options.case: Product clarity holds for asynchronous scan changes; audience identification is weaker because travel ordering differs from prospect retrieval.
options.risk: Live reranking can disrupt review, so sorting changes remain explicit and reduced motion preserves row identity.

options.label: Tabbed software manual
options.lineage: Boxed-software reference manuals and section dividers
options.thesis: Each research task occupies a clear section with its own persistent tab.
options.viewport: Discover is the current divider; readable record leaves sit above its color board with scope controls and evidence ordered as reference entries.
options.case: Audience identification holds through software documentation; product clarity loses when layered sections compete with dense comparison.
options.risk: Layered materials need strict contrast; standard labels replace holes/face-down states and motion reduces to brief task feedback.

options.label: Factory catalog sleeve
options.thesis: Each business becomes a numbered catalog artifact with decoded source and website evidence.
options.viewport: A stable record number anchors the selected business; an index and explicitly decoded labels organize source facts and website evidence.
options.case: Loses audience identification and product clarity: numbered art objects add interpretation to finding named local businesses.
options.kept: Stable record identity and a complete, consistent hierarchy across all surfaces.
options.risk: Coded colors cannot replace accessible source/status text; plots must use actual permitted data.

options.label: Streaming catalog wall
options.lineage: Streaming-library rows and focused title details
options.thesis: Category rows reveal a business's full evidence when its tile is selected.
options.viewport: Business categories form keyboard-accessible rows; selection expands website/source facts using text records without unlicensed business photos.
options.case: Loses audience identification and product clarity: horizontal rails and hidden metadata slow bulk prospect comparison.
options.kept: Complete focused evidence without losing result context, with equal keyboard/touch access.
options.risk: Source imagery is absent and unlicensed; focus expansion must not require hover or hide essential comparison fields.

options.label: Datamatics field
options.lineage: Monochrome data-art lattices and numeric columns
options.thesis: Dense columns expose actual scan counts and evidence rather than a decorative dashboard.
options.viewport: Actual permitted scan statistics align with a selected business column; explicit labels and static data views replace strobing.
options.case: Loses audience identification and product clarity: artistic frequency navigation adds little to business retrieval or prospect decisions.
options.kept: Real information density, aligned figures and honest unknowns.
options.risk: No strobing or decorative fabricated data; the task must remain readable and accessible at all sizes.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A conventional CRM dashboard with sidebar, statistics, filters and table.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar navigation, compact statistics, search/filter toolbar and a full-width prospect table with a detail drawer.
canonCard.risk: Familiar by design; choose this if the product should sit alongside conventional CRMs.
